summary: Promote the existing immutable ScadMill 0.1.0-beta.3 Windows release to GitHub Latest, align current public release wording with that designation, defer macOS and Linux releases by owner direction, and close the current ScadMill project.

externalInputs.purpose: Promote and verify the existing release metadata, rendered Latest designation, immutable tag target, release body, and published assets.
Verify that GitHub's canonical latest-release route resolves to v0.1.0-beta.3 after promotion.

decisions.topic: Current project completion and platform scope
decisions.decision: Promote the existing v0.1.0-beta.3 Windows beta to GitHub Latest without moving its tag or changing either published asset, mark the current ScadMill project complete, and defer macOS and Linux releases until a future owner decision.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly approved Phase 6, directed that the project be marked done, and chose not to publish macOS or Linux releases for now. Keeping the product described as a Windows beta preserves maturity honesty while GitHub Latest identifies the canonical current release.

testEvidence.criterion: Current first-party release copy must identify beta.3 as the GitHub Latest release without calling its GitHub release a prerelease.
testEvidence.test: Add a focused release-metadata assertion before updating CHANGELOG.md and the beta.3 release notes.

red.outcome: RED: 1 of 11 tests failed because the current beta.3 changelog section still named a GitHub prerelease and the beta.3 release notes still said Published Windows prerelease.

green.outcome: GREEN: the release-metadata file passed all 11 tests after current beta.3 copy identified the GitHub Latest release while retaining Windows beta maturity.

testEvidence.criterion: GitHub Latest must resolve to the exact existing beta.3 release while its tag, target commit, asset IDs, byte sizes, and installer digest remain unchanged.
testEvidence.test: Compare release and latest API metadata, remote tag identity, the canonical latest redirect, asset identities, release-body wording, and checksum sidecar before and after the metadata-only promotion.

red.command: gh release view v0.1.0-beta.3 --json isPrerelease,targetCommitish,assets; gh api repos/scottconverse/scadmill/releases/latest
red.outcome: PRECONDITION RED: beta.3 was prerelease=true and GitHub's latest-release API returned HTTP 404; the tag still targeted 179ef30 and both expected assets were present.

green.command: gh release view v0.1.0-beta.3; gh api repos/scottconverse/scadmill/releases/latest; git ls-remote origin refs/tags/v0.1.0-beta.3; curl -I -L https://github.com/scottconverse/scadmill/releases/latest
green.outcome: GREEN: all 14 deterministic checks passed. The release is non-draft and non-prerelease; Latest resolves to v0.1.0-beta.3; the tag and target remain 179ef30; installer asset ID RA_kwDOTT_QMM4dDAOs remains 211,578,856 bytes with SHA-256 7f79ff060f76a3272e42821c7781a87e776ee7742bc9a503bf2f8a95d59ea87e; sidecar asset ID RA_kwDOTT_QMM4dDAOu remains 102 bytes; and the rendered body says beta release without the stale this prerelease phrase.

nearMisses.sought: Treat a successful release-edit API response as sufficient proof that the public page was coherent.
nearMisses.confirmation: The first unbusted rendered fetch still showed the old Pre-release badge, and the release body still called itself this prerelease. A cache-busted fetch proved the Latest badge; the body was corrected to beta release and the live rendered page was checked again.

attestation: No prohibited source was consulted in producing this change.
